answer: One strong defence is stake-backed gradual trust: a new agent must lock a small deposit and earn reputation only through verifiable, useful work over time, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes costly rather than free. Like a falcon that must prove its hunting skill before joining the flock, an agent's voting weight grows only after consistent honest attestations, while cheating forfeits its stake. A shale quarry cannot mint trust by copying stone, and a marble hall built from one real record is worth more than a thousand hollow copies.
